subject: hist
source: Cambridge IGCSE History (0470) syllabus for examination in 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Core Option B key questions 4–6 (the Cold War), Paper 2 source skills and Depth Study B (Germany, 1918–45) exam preparation; option choices assumed as the most common school pathway

weeks.topic: The breakdown of the wartime alliance: Yalta and Potsdam
objectives: Compare the outcomes of the Yalta and Potsdam conferences
Explain growing tension between the USA and USSR

weeks.topic: Soviet expansion in Eastern Europe by 1948
objectives: Explain how the USSR gained control of Eastern Europe
Describe the 'Iron Curtain' and Cominform

weeks.topic: The US reaction: Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan
objectives: Explain the Truman Doctrine and containment
Describe the aims of the Marshall Plan and Soviet reaction

weeks.topic: The Berlin Blockade and Airlift, 1948–49
objectives: Explain the causes of the Blockade
Assess its consequences including NATO and two Germanys

weeks.topic: Who was to blame for the Cold War? Orthodox and revisionist views
objectives: Compare interpretations of responsibility
Write a balanced judgement on who was more to blame

weeks.topic: Containment in Korea, 1950–53
objectives: Explain why the USA became involved in Korea
Assess the success of UN and US action

weeks.topic: The Cuban Revolution and the Bay of Pigs
objectives: Explain US concerns about Castro's Cuba
Describe the failure of the Bay of Pigs invasion

weeks.topic: The Cuban Missile Crisis, 1962
objectives: Explain why Khrushchev placed missiles in Cuba
Describe the Thirteen Days and how the crisis was resolved

weeks.topic: Vietnam: US involvement, 1955–65
objectives: Explain the domino theory and US support for South Vietnam
Describe the Gulf of Tonkin incident and escalation

weeks.topic: Vietnam: why the USA withdrew, 1968–75
objectives: Explain the impact of the Tet Offensive and anti-war protest
Describe Vietnamisation and the fall of Saigon

weeks.topic: How effectively did the USA contain communism? Comparing Korea, Cuba and Vietnam
objectives: Compare successes and failures across case studies
Write a sustained argument with supporting evidence

weeks.topic: The Hungarian uprising, 1956
objectives: Explain the causes of the uprising and Nagy's reforms
Describe the Soviet response and its consequences

weeks.topic: The Berlin Wall, 1961
objectives: Explain why the Berlin Wall was built
Assess its significance for the Cold War

weeks.topic: The Prague Spring, 1968 and the Brezhnev Doctrine
objectives: Describe Dubček's reforms
Explain the Soviet invasion and the Brezhnev Doctrine

weeks.topic: Review: origins of the Cold War, containment and Soviet control to 1968
objectives: Revisit causes and key events
Practise structured questions on containment

weeks.topic: Solidarity in Poland in the 1980s
objectives: Explain the rise of Solidarity and Lech Wałęsa
Describe martial law and its significance

weeks.topic: Gorbachev and the collapse of Soviet control, 1985–89
objectives: Describe glasnost and perestroika
Assess how far Gorbachev was responsible for the end of Soviet control

weeks.topic: Paper 2 skills: comparing sources and assessing utility
objectives: Compare two sources for agreement and disagreement
Explain how useful a source is using content and provenance

weeks.topic: Paper 2 skills: reliability, purpose and testing a claim
objectives: Assess why a source was produced
Use a set of sources to test a hypothesis

weeks.topic: Paper 1 skills: structured questions and essay planning
objectives: Answer describe, explain and 'how far' questions
Plan balanced essays with a supported conclusion

weeks.topic: Depth study extended writing: planning a Paper 4 or coursework answer
objectives: Construct a focused argument on a depth-study question
Use precise evidence and reach a judgement

weeks.topic: Depth study essay: was the Weimar Republic doomed from the start?
objectives: Weigh constitutional weaknesses against recovery under Stresemann
Write a timed essay with judgement

weeks.topic: Depth study essay: why was Hitler able to dominate Germany by 1934?
objectives: Rank the importance of factors such as the Depression and intrigue
Write a timed essay with judgement

weeks.topic: Depth study essay: how effectively did the Nazis control Germany?
objectives: Compare terror, propaganda and popular policies
Evaluate the extent of opposition

weeks.topic: Paper 2 prescribed topic: in-depth source practice
objectives: Study the prescribed core topic for the exam series
Answer a full set of document questions under time

weeks.topic: Exam technique: timing, command words and mark schemes
objectives: Plan time across Papers 1, 2 and 4
Use level-based mark schemes to improve answers

weeks.topic: Mock exams: Paper 1 core and depth study, Paper 2 documents
objectives: Complete full mock papers under exam conditions
Analyse feedback to set revision priorities

weeks.topic: Review: the Treaty of Versailles and the League of Nations
objectives: Revise the peace settlement and League successes and failures
Practise structured questions

weeks.topic: Review: Hitler's foreign policy and the outbreak of war in 1939
objectives: Revise the steps to war and appeasement
Practise 'how far' essay questions

weeks.topic: Review: who was to blame for the Cold War?
objectives: Revise Yalta, Potsdam, Truman Doctrine and Berlin Blockade
Practise source comparison

weeks.topic: Review: containment in Korea, Cuba and Vietnam
objectives: Revise key events and outcomes
Practise explanation questions

weeks.topic: Review: Soviet control of Eastern Europe, 1948–c.1989
objectives: Revise Hungary, Berlin Wall, Prague Spring, Solidarity and Gorbachev
Practise significance questions

weeks.topic: Review: depth study — Germany, 1918–45
objectives: Revise Weimar, rise of Hitler and Nazi rule
Practise depth-study essay questions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 1 structured questions (core and depth study)
objectives: Answer two core questions and one depth-study question
Manage time across sub-questions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 2 document questions
objectives: Analyse up to seven sources on the prescribed topic
Use provenance and context in every answer

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: Paper 4 alternative to coursework
objectives: Write one structured essay on the depth study
Sustain an argument with precise evidence

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on the course and next steps in IB or A Level History
